meta.title: Competitor Radar
meta.niche: US sales tax compliance software for mid-market ecommerce and SaaS brands

analysis.summary: TaxCloud leads on switching content: 14 comparison pages and 16 case studies. Rivals mostly publish learning content, like state guides, webinars and city rate pages.

points.text: TaxCloud's 14 comparison pages and 16 case studies target people ready to switch, and no rival matches that mix.
Avalara's 84 pages are mostly webinars and product news, with only 3 aimed at buyers. It is not defending against switchers here.
TaxJar (77 pages) and Kintsugi (461) publish mostly state-by-state how-tos, aimed at people learning. Kintsugi also has 5 comparison pages, some aimed at Avalara users.

shared.title: State-by-state tax guides
shared.text: TaxJar and Kintsugi mass-produce state and topic guides, such as shipping tax and rates and rules. They catch early researchers. TaxCloud has few of these.

shared.title: Rival-pricing and alternatives pages
shared.text: Zamp and Kintsugi write pages on Avalara and TaxJar pricing and alternatives. They are going after TaxCloud's switcher audience.

shared.title: SaaS tax content
shared.text: Anrok and Kintsugi both publish SaaS taxability guides, including California's new SaaS tax. TaxCloud has one SaaS guide and a SaaS software roundup.

gaps.title: Switching playbook hub
gaps.text: Only Anrok has a switching-platform guide, and TaxCloud has two how-tos. A full hub with checklists, timelines and migration stories could own this.

gaps.title: State taxability guides for ecommerce
gaps.text: TaxJar and Kintsugi cover states one page at a time. TaxCloud could add mid-market guides that end in a migration offer.

gaps.title: Tariff and trade tax for ecommerce
gaps.text: Only Avalara covers tariffs, and it does so through webinars. TaxCloud could publish written explainers for ecommerce sellers.
